card.name: Buyo (Nihon Buyo)
card.era: Formalized Edo period (1603-1867); term coined Meiji period
card.tagline: Classical Japanese theatrical dance derived from kabuki
card.profile: Nihon-buyo ('Japanese dance') is the classical Japanese performing art of theatrical dance. It developed from earlier mai and odori traditions and was shaped during the early Edo period through kabuki dance (shosagoto), combining mai (soft, undulating movement), odori (rhythmic steps) and furi (gesture) to shamisen accompaniment, performed in kimono with fans and other props (Wikipedia, Nihon-buyo). The term dates to the Meiji period; the repertoire centres on kabuki dance plays such as Kyoganoko Musume Dojoji and Fuji Musume (Wisteria Maiden).
card.insight: Per the Hanayagi Dancing Academy Hawaii Foundation, nihon buyo is 'dominated by five major schools' - Hanayagi, Fujima, Nishikawa, Bando and Wakayagi - of which the Hanayagi-ryu is the largest, with an estimated 20,000 licensed members (among roughly 200 schools in total).
